question.problem:
Given that the function

$$
g(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\sqrt{b-3x}+2, & x\le 0 \\ x+3, & x>0\end{aligned}
$$

is continuous at $x=0$, find the value of the constant $b.$
question.worked_solution:
At $x=0,$ the left-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {0}^{-}}g(x) & =g(0) \\  & =\sqrt{b-3(0)}+2 \\  & =\sqrt{b}+2,\end{aligned}
$$

 

and the right-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}g(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}(x+3) \\  & =0+3 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for $f(x)$ to be continuous at $x=0,$ we require that

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {0}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}f(x) \\ \sqrt{b}+2 & =3 \\ \sqrt{b} & =3-2 \\ \sqrt{b} & =1 \\ b & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
